title: Security Deposit Anniversary Interest: Cash on Which Interest Is Earned
content:
The cash on which a Security Deposit earns interest for the year credited on its anniversary depends on the refunds and payments shown among the deposit's transactions.

| Deposit's transactions | Interest is earned on |
|---|---|
| An excess refund has been paid out of the deposit, and no deposit payment was received in the year being credited | The cash received less the excess refunds paid |
| A deposit payment was received in the year being credited | The cash held when the year began plus one half of the payments received in the year |
| Neither of the above | The cash received |

**Terms.** The cash received is the total of the deposit payments received on the deposit. An excess refund is a refund paid out of a held deposit after a recalculation lowered its required amount. The payments of the year being credited are counted over the 12 months ending on the day the credit is booked, which is the anniversary.

## Hypothetical cases

1. A deposit has received USD 6000.00 in payments, an excess refund of USD 800.00 was paid out of it, and no payment was received in the 12 months ending on the anniversary. Interest is earned on USD 5200.00.
2. A deposit held USD 1000.00 in cash when the year began, with no refunds, and received a further USD 400.00 payment during the year. Interest is earned on USD 1000.00 plus one half of USD 400.00, that is USD 1200.00.
3. A deposit has received USD 480.00 in payments, all before the year began, and nothing has been refunded. Interest is earned on USD 480.00.
